title.narrative: Offensive against Al-Shabaab in Southwest and Jubaland

description.narrative:
This project is a research project on how clan and local political dynamics may affect the likelihood for success of the current efforts to counter, degrade and “eliminate” al Shabaab as a threat, and strengthen government presence in today’s al Shabaab controlled areas, focusing on South West State and Jubaland State, with comparison to current developments in Hirshabelle and Galmudug State. The research is based on questions developed by Raad. The research will take place in Mogadishu, Kismayo and Baidoa, including data collection and interviews. The project will produce one open policy brief that provides analyses relevant to Somalia’s and the international community’s understanding of the topic, for a wider audience, plus a brief for the Somali government and relevant international partners.
Outputs: 1. Policy brief tailored to the wider public, ATMIS, and UNSOM, and international partners 2. Detailed report to the FGS 3. Workshop in Halane
Outcomes: 1. Better insights and understanding of how the FGS and its FMS can establish a sustainable and legitimate presence in the eyes of the locals and clans to stabilise these two regions 2. Clarifying potential ways international actors can support this stablisation process
